title: Caching public reads
summary: A service reads the network only through an `HTTPClient`; a JavaScript or TypeScript service that calls `fetch` itself fails to build with `TY1361`. To keep a read, put the cache annotations that services use on the client, as Spring's `@Cacheable` works on any bean: `CacheSettings` on the client class names the cache and its limits, `Cached` on a read keeps its answer (with `CacheKey` on the arguments that pick the answer), and `ClearCache` or `UpdateCache` on a write removes or replaces that answer after the write succeeds. This works the same in every language that has an `HTTPClient`. Python and Lua have no tab here, because the build refuses `HTTPClient` in Python and Lua Tac code with `TY1308`. In JavaScript and TypeScript, Tachyon's browser transport also sends a `Cached` GET as a public read, so the service worker may answer it. A service worker is a browser script that can answer requests from a cache. The manifest's `tac.cache` sets the worker's policy for each path: `cache-first`, `network-first` or `no-store`. A path without a rule is not kept by the worker. The worker keeps a read only when it has no `Authorization` header and the response is cacheable; a response with `private`, `no-store` or `Vary` is not kept, and a successful write removes the entries under its path. After `ClearCache` or `UpdateCache`, the next uncached JavaScript or TypeScript GET revalidates the browser HTTP cache, even when the server sent a long public `max-age`; a cache-first worker rule also asks the network for that read. A read that is not `Cached` is sent `no-store`, so it is always fresh. A GET that sends an `Authorization` header is never kept in the browser HTTP cache, even when it is `Cached`. Dart, Rust, Go, Kotlin, Swift, Java, Ruby, C# and F# clients use the same browser transport when their Setup has no HTTP adapter for the client. C++ has an `HTTPClient` but no tab here, because a C++ `HTTPClient` method cannot carry `Cached` yet (ADR 0099). In the compiled examples below, the Setup's HTTP adapter answers inside the page, so the worker never sees the request, and `Cached` keeps the answer in the page. The old `cache` option of `@HTTPClient` is replaced by `Cached` (ADR 0087).
